### Non-Obvious Implementation Notes

1. **Email compose overlay pattern:** The email compose panel sits INSIDE the center column and pushes the timeline down — it is NOT a modal overlay. The timeline is still accessible by scrolling. When closed (e.g., trash icon clicked), the compose panel collapses and the timeline expands to fill the space.

2. **Recipient chip from URL context:** The "To: Laurie McAdam" chip is pre-populated because the compose panel was opened from within this person's record. The FUB email client knows the contact's email address from `lgmcadam@gmail.com`.

3. **Email signature injection:** The broker's HTML email signature is injected into the compose body automatically when the compose panel opens. It is editable (the rich text editor allows deleting/modifying it). The signature is stored on the user/broker profile, not the contact.

4. **Template tabs pre-fill logic:** Clicking a template tab (Introduction, Follow Up, etc.) replaces the current Subject and Body content with a stored template, but preserves the recipient. The "Custom" tab likely opens a template manager.

5. **Timeline filter counts:** The counts in the filter tabs (3 emails, 1 forward, 1 text, 4 drip events) are computed from the full timeline for this contact, regardless of which filter is active. The "All" tab shows all events interleaved by date.

6. **Person 2 of 9 navigation context:** This context comes from the list/smart list that the user was viewing before clicking into this contact detail. FUB maintains a "current list" in the browser state, allowing prev/next navigation within the list. The keyboard shortcuts [↓]/[↑] persist even while the compose panel is open.

7. **Overdue task coloring:** Task due dates in the past are rendered in orange text (not red). Tasks approaching within e.g. 24h may render in yellow/amber [INFERRED from FUB conventions].

8. **Lead Origin note generation:** The "LEAD ORIGIN" note in the timeline is auto-generated by a FUB webhook/API integration when a new lead comes in. It is created as a system note attributed to the assigned agent (Matt Ryan). The structured format (key: value line-by-line) is a convention in this Ryan Realty implementation.

9. **AgentFire FUB Widget:** This is a third-party integration panel injected into the right sidebar via FUB's widget/integration API. The collapsed state indicates it may require additional configuration or the contact has no matching data in AgentFire's system.

10. **"Seen 17 days ago" in Activity:** This likely refers to when the contact last visited the Ryan Realty website (tracked via pixel/GA4 integration with FUB), not when the agent last viewed this record.

11. **Automation pause icon:** The two-bar pause icon next to "Web Inquiry Option 01" allows stopping the drip sequence mid-run for this specific contact without deleting the automation configuration globally.

12. **Files section — drag-and-drop:** The empty state "No files yet, drag some here" indicates the section is a drop target for native browser drag-and-drop file uploads. Standard HTML5 drag-and-drop implementation pointing to a FUB file storage API.

13. **"Marketing Emails" button/tooltip:** This appears to be a toggle or secondary send path that routes the email through FUB's mass-email/drip system rather than the agent's personal inbox — useful for tracking opens/clicks with marketing analytics rather than 1:1 personal email attribution.
